chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When a man is upon a deed, let him persist upon it for a year. Then he should change from it, if Allah wills, to something else. And that is because the Night of Pre-determination (Laylat al-Qadr) will occur in it during that year of his, whatever Allah wills to be.
ai.seo_question: How long should one persist in a specific act of worship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this advice from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the spiritual discipline of consistency (istiqarah), suggesting that maintaining a specific practice for a year allows one to capture the blessings of Laylat al-Qadr within that annual cycle. This period serves as a test of perseverance, ensuring that the deed is not merely a fleeting impulse but a sustained commitment that aligns with divine decree.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the man was upon a (particular) deed, so let him persist upon it for a year. Then he should change from it, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing, to something else, and that is because the Night of Pre-determination (Laylat Al-Qadr) would occur in it during that year of his. Whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires would transpire’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘If a man does a good deed, he should continue for a year before ending, if he may so wish, to perform another good deed. This is because the night of destiny comes in his year in which things that Allah wills come into being.’”
